cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.heading: False or Misleading Benefit Presentation
cases.claim: Video prominently communicates that Trulicity can help “lower A1C along with diet and exercise,” but fails to adequately communicate the FDA-approved indication and limitations of use.
cases.context: Indication/limitations only in small fast-scrolling font in a window at bottom, competing with fast visuals, scene changes, moving text and music. Bad Ad complaint; prior advisory comments.
cases.rationale: Implies Trulicity lowers A1C in all patients; omits limitations (not for T1D/DKA, pancreatitis, severe GI disease).
cases.check: Rule: limitations of use from the label must appear with comparable prominence to the first benefit claim.

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: Risk information in a small window relegated to the bottom of the post, presented using fast-paced, scrolling, small font, while benefit claims use colorful, fast-paced visuals, large-moving superimposed text and a strong, fast-moving musical beat.
cases.rationale: Risk not presented with comparable prominence and readability.
cases.check: Rule: flag social video where risk appears only in a scrolling sub-window or small font relative to benefit text.

cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: Fails to include: “Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Your risk for getting low blood sugar may be higher if you use TRULICITY with another medicine that can cause low blood sugar, such as a sulfonylurea or insulin.”
cases.check: Rule: verify W&P conditional risks (e.g., with concomitant drugs) are stated, not just the risk name.
